A few regex edge cases still differ from JavaScript and are documented on `JSRegExp`. They are: a back reference to a group that took no part, which fails here but matches the empty string in JavaScript; `\P{Lu}` under the `i` flag; the captures of empty loops such as `(a*)*` and `(|a)+`; look-behinds that are not of bounded length; and a ligature such as ﬁ inside a character class also matching 'fi'.
A saved text setting cut at 255 UTF-16 units inside a surrogate pair leaves U+FFFD here, where JavaScript keeps half the pair, because a Swift String cannot hold a lone surrogate.
The reference runs on Bun's JavaScriptCore, not V8, so the goldens record JSC's regex behaviour. The two engines are not known to differ on the tested patterns, but I did not check against V8.

2. **Realpath and stream start on the main thread.** `FSEventsFolderWatcher.watchFolder` now returns a stop function immediately. One behavior difference from the reference: a folder that can't be watched (missing, say) used to give nil, so nothing was reported until the next watch() or focus retry. findings.evidence: Node sorts the rendered entry strings, not the raw keys, and quotes any key that is not /^[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z_0-9]*$/. The port sorts raw keys (LogFormat.swift, `members.keys.sorted()`), treats `$` and non-ASCII letters as bare identifiers (inspectKey, `$0 == "$" || $0.properties.isAlphabetic`), and puts no quote character first in the sort. I ran the reference with `node -e 'const {inspect}=require("util");console.log(inspect({a:1,a1:2,"a-b":3,b:4,$x:5},{depth:8,breakLength:Infinity,compact:true,sorted:true}))'`. It prints `{ '$x': 5, 'a-b': 3, a1: 2, a: 1, b: 4 }`. The port's algorithm gives `{ a: 1, a-b: ... }`: raw-key sort gives a, a-b, a1, b, $x. It also writes `$x` unquoted and `a-b` with the wrong quoting or order. Keys such as `a`/`a1` order differently because ':' (0x3a) sorts after digits in the rendered `key: value` strings. The same applies to `$`-prefixed and quoted keys, which sort first because of the leading quote. Writing structured entries (`write(level:namespace:message:context:)`) with such context keys gives a different app.log line than the reference. No test covers this: Tests/FTFileSystemTests/Logging/AppLoggerTests.swift has no `sorted` or inspect-ordering case. Reproduce the port side with a Swift test calling `LogFormat.arguments([.context(["a":.number(1),"a1":.number(2),"$x":.number(5)])])` and comparing to `{ '$x': 5, a1: 2, a: 1 }`.

findings.where: Sources/FTOperations/Analysis/CopyPasteAnalysis.swift:377-378 (NodeWalker.analyzeNode, childSourcePath/childDestinationPath), which calls Sources/FTFoundation/Names/NodePath.swift:84-117 (join -> normalize: an Array of Unicode.Scalar per path component, then a rebuilt String)
findings.evidence:
Benchmark on the same input: a 150,000-file folder ("/source/project/files/file-N-with-a-longer-name.txt") copied to "/target", each tool called directly, in release builds.

In memory (an exact-path mock like Tests/FTOperationsTests/Analysis/LargeTreeAnalysisTests.swift:13):
- Reference: ~/Library/Caches/filetrail-port/reference/electron/packages/core/src/fs/copyPasteAnalysis.ts buildCopyPasteAnalysisReport, run with `bun run scratchpad/bench.ts`, prints "TS analysis ms 270".
- Port: buildCopyPasteAnalysisReport compiled with `swiftc -O` against .build/release FTOperations.o, FTFoundation.o, FTFileSystem.o and CFileTrail.o, prints "Swift release analysis 1.34 seconds" (3 runs: 1.36, 1.34, 1.32).

On a real APFS disk (the same 150k files written in the scratchpad):
- Port with PosixFileSystem(): 4.16, 4.09, 4.17 s.
- Reference with node:fs/promises lstat, stat, realpath, readdir and readlink: 4.46, 3.75, 3.82 s.

`sample` of the port during the real-disk run:
- ReportBuilder.build: 3248 samples in total.
- CopyPasteAnalysis.swift:377 NodePath.join: 1302 samples.
- CopyPasteAnalysis.swift:378 NodePath.join: 1216 samples.
- Together that is 2518 of 3248 (77%), nearly all at NodePath.swift:86 normalize (String.UnicodeScalarView.append, Array allocation and free).
- lstat in captureFingerprint at lines 346 and 348 is only about 330 samples.
- The in-memory run shows the same split: 3354 of 4062 samples (82%) are in these two joins.

The reference's per-child cost is node:path.join, which is a cheap native string operation. Here every one of the 150k items allocates about 2 x (components + 2) arrays. The child name comes from readdir and the parent is already normalized, so `parent + "/" + name` (with "/" as the special case, as joinChildDestinationPath in CopyPasteResolution.swift:213 already does) would give the same output.

Impact:
- The port reviews a large paste no faster than the Electron app, and slightly slower than the reference running under bun, though the plan expects native to be faster.
- The report also costs CPU on the review thread in proportion to the item count.
- Analysis runs off the main thread, so no UI budget is broken. The cost is review latency and CPU.

findings.evidence: Reference: reloadFolderAfterOutsideChange (hooks/useExplorerNavigationController.ts:1976-1984) marks the changed paths stale. The loader (same file :2224-2229) keeps what is shown for a stale item (comment: 'An item that changed on disk keeps what is shown for it until it is read again'). Port: show(...) does `metadata[changed] = nil` (:278), or `metadata = [:]` when changedPaths is nil (:280). ListCellText returns "" for nil metadata (Content/List/ListCellText.swift: detailSize, kind, date, permissions). So Kind, Modified, Size and Permissions go blank until the async metadata batch returns (flicker). A save to one file blanks that row, and a full re-read blanks every row. findings.title: Folder-watch change paths are dropped, so every outside change is treated as 'anything may have changed'
findings.evidence: Reference: useFolderWatch.ts:68-70 passes the merged changedPaths (null only if unknown or more than 1000) to reload, and only those items' details are marked stale (useExplorerNavigationController.ts:1978). Port: FolderWatches delivers FolderChange{path, changedPaths} (FTFileSystem/Listing/ListingTypes.swift:117-121). `ExplorerWindows.folderChanged(windowID:_ change:)` ignores `change` and calls `tab(windowID:)?.reload()`, so changedPaths defaults to nil. PendingChange.merging therefore always yields nil. The 'changed items only' path in ContentPaneController.show (:276-279) and `pane?.refresh(paths:)` (:299) is never used in the app, so a one-file change re-reads and blanks the details of every row (see the previous finding). Fix: `reload(changedPaths: change.changedPaths)`.

fixes.summary:
Fixed at 56ae0deed1174953dbc646ef868a9763280181fa on port/P0-13. The intermittent failure never reproduced for me, so the cause is inferred and the new test is not a failing-first test. Both gates pass: 8 filtered iterations, then scripts/ci.sh (940 tests, 0 failures). I also ran scripts/ci.sh six times beforehand with no failure.

Likely cause: the test checked `!isMounted(folder.path)`, a mount-path check. Between the eject and that check, another process can attach a clone of the same blank image and take the freed `/Volumes/<name>`. Candidates are another worktree's test run on older code without the cross-process lock, or ExecPlaces' unlocked attaches. The path then shows mounted even though our volume is gone.

The fix is in `Tests/FTFileSystemTests/Volumes/VolumeEjectorTests.swift`. The tests now record the volume's device node (`/dev/diskNsM`) before ejecting and assert that device is no longer mounted. The same change applies to the other three eject tests that checked the path.

Earlier commits on the branch already cover the thumbnail flakiness, the per-kind disk-image `flock`, and the listing bench metrics.

ExecDiskImages in `Tests/FTTestSupport/ExecPlaces.swift` still attaches clones of the same blank images without the per-kind lock. It holds them until process exit, so locking it would hang `DiskImage.withVolume`. If the flake returns, look there first.

openIssues.history: P5-01 (6b6a9d9) removed the window's NSSplitViewController and replaced NSToolbar (PLAN §3.5's choice) with a custom toolbar view under a transparent title bar. Its reasons: the unified NSToolbar band measured 66 pt (compact 40), not the original's 52; NSToolbar's insets, overflow and sidebar separator couldn't match; and Customize Toolbar edits in place as the original does. Removing the split view controller is what put the tab bar over the sidebar. In the 2026-10-14 spike, a unified, icon-only NSToolbar with a sidebar split measured 52 pt (NSToolbarView 448..500 in a 500 pt window), so the follow-up WP should re-check the 66 pt claim before keeping the custom toolbar. Either way, the tab bar placement needs only the NSSplitViewController with a sidebar item; a custom toolbar band inside the content item still works.
